question: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a deliberative assembly?

options.A: The size of the group is less than six.
options.B: Members can participate and act on their own judgment.
options.C: The group meets and after full and free discussion decides action to be taken.
options.D: Each member's vote has equal weight.

question: The questions acted upon in a deliberative assembly are normally decided by the

options.B: members who are present at a regular meeting.
options.C: members who vote by mail.

question: An assembly is a

options.A: session of an executive board of a larger organization.
options.B: special meeting of the members of an organization.
options.C: body of people who come together as a group.

question: A member of an assembly, in a parliamentary sense, is a person having the right to

options.A: examine all the records of the organization.
options.B: attend the executive sessions.
options.C: participate fully in its proceedings.
options.D: debate a motion in detail before it is proposed.

question: Members of a deliberative assembly

options.B: may vote only if their dues are paid.
options.C: have the right to make motions, participate in debate, and vote.
options.D: can stop debate on any motion by yelling out "Question!"

question: A deliberative assembly that has not adopted rules to govern its organization is bound by the rules and customs

options.A: of the constitution of its State Legislature.
options.B: that were drafted by the officers prior to the first meeting.
options.C: of common parliamentary law.

question: The actions of any deliberative assembly are subject to

options.A: only the rules of the parent organization.
options.B: change by a majority vote of the members without notice.
options.C: the bylaws and other rules of its organization and all applicable local, state, and national laws.
options.D: change by the president and secretary of the organization.

question: The basic principle of decision in a deliberative assembly is that

options.A: propositions must be adopted by a majority vote.
options.B: it takes two members to demand a rising vote.
options.C: a two-thirds vote is required for all amendments.
options.D: all the decisions of the presiding officer may be reversed by a two-thirds vote.

question: In a deliberative assembly, a proposition may be adopted by a majority vote, which means that a motion must be approved by

options.A: all the members present who vote.
options.B: two-thirds of the voting members.
options.C: more than half of the members present and voting.
options.D: exactly half of the members in the organization.

question: When an organization needs to make a decision that requires more than a majority vote, common requirements are a

options.B: ballot vote.
options.C: two-thirds vote and possibly previous notice.

question: The call of a meeting is a

options.B: demand by the presiding officer for the meeting to begin.
options.C: written notice of the time and place of the meeting which is sent to all members in advance.
options.D: verbal notice of the time and place of the meeting at least one year prior to the date of the meeting.

question: Which of the following would not be classified as a principal type of deliberative assembly?

options.B: Convention
options.C: Board

question: When an unorganized group meets to discuss a specific problem and anyone may attend who is interested, it is called a

options.B: mass meeting.
options.C: legislative body.

question: Admittance to a mass meeting

options.B: may not be limited.
options.C: may be limited.
options.D: is determined by membership to the society that is conducting the meeting.

question: Membership in a local assembly of an organized society is limited to persons who are

options.A: listed in the rolls of the society as voting members in good standing.
options.B: in attendance at meetings.
options.C: always chosen by its president.

question: The bylaws of an organized local society usually provide that it shall hold

options.B: regular meetings at stated intervals.
options.C: a specific number of meetings each year.

question: Which type of deliberative assembly below is characterized by having each meeting normally serve as a separate session?

options.B: Legislative body
options.C: Organized local societies

question: An assembly of delegates normally chosen for one session is called a

options.B: board.
options.C: convention.

question: Which one of the following statements is true regarding a convention?

options.A: A convention is never called to form an association.
options.B: The voting membership of a convention usually consists of delegates.
options.C: Ordinary conventions last a month.
options.D: The Credentials Committee certifies all non-delegates.

question: When a convention concludes,

options.A: official delegates must meet to elect new officers.
options.B: the assembly is normally dissolved
options.D: all of the officers may meet to adopt new bylaws.
options.C: alternate delegates begin their own convention.

question: Law-making groups such as Congress are called

options.B: legislative bodies.
options.C: congressional boards.

question: A board is an administrative body that is

options.B: appointed at a general meeting by the chairman.
options.C: elected or appointed.

question: A board generally has the same character of a

options.B: deliberative assembly.
options.C: large committee.

question: The minimum size of a board is

options.D: None of the above. Boards have no minimum size and are usually smaller than assemblies.

question: A board within an organized society

options.A: such as a board of education may be assigned a particular function.
options.B: has responsibilities that are conferred on it by authority outside itself.
options.C: is subordinate to the society's full assembly.

question: Large boards follow parliamentary procedure

options.A: in the same way as any assembly.
options.B: to a lesser degree than other deliberative assemblies.
options.C: only for items that are brought from the previous meeting.
options.D: when the presiding officer feels it will benefit the organization.

question: An organized society requires certain rules to

options.A: establish its basic structure and manner of operation.
options.B: make certain it is different from other societies.
options.C: allow its officers to rule against its bylaws.
options.D: ensure that its officers are not liable for their actions.

question: What is the legal document that gives the name and object of a society and also other information as required by law?

options.B: Constitution
options.C: Bylaws

question: The Corporate Charter of a society that wishes to be incorporated should contain

options.B: the object of the society.
options.C: any information required of the particular state where the society originated.

question: One principal advantage of incorporating a society is that the officers and members

options.A: can deduct expenses from their state income taxes while serving the organization.
options.B: can change the bylaws without a vote of the members.
options.C: are protected from personal liability under obligations that may be incurred by the organization.
options.D: use the facilities of the organization for their personal profit.

question: A corporate charter should be drafted by

options.A: the first officers of an organization.
options.B: a special committee.
options.C: an attorney.
options.D: the Constitution Committee of the organization.

question: In an incorporated organization, the document that supersedes all other rules is the

options.B: bylaws and the constitution.
options.C: corporate charter.
options.D: business license from the state where the organization originated.

question: The document of a society that contains its own rules relating to itself as an organization is the

options.B: standing committee report.
options.C: corporate charter.

question: The first two articles in the bylaws of an unincorporated society are

options.B: Members and Officers.
options.C: The Name of the Organization and its Object.
options.D: The Parliamentary Authority and Executive Board.

question: Which article below is generally not included in an organization's bylaws?

options.B: Parliamentary authority
options.C: Officers
options.D: A listing of all the members' legal names and addresses

question: An incorporated society

options.A: should have the charter, bylaws, and constitution combined.
options.B: is not different from an unincorporated society.
options.C: should have a separate constitution and bylaws.
options.D: should not have the constitution separated from the bylaws.

question: Except for the corporate charter in an incorporated society, the highest body of rules are the

options.B: standing rules.
options.C: laws of the federal government.

question: The written rules of parliamentary procedure formally adopted by an assembly or an organization are known as the

options.B: certificate of endorsement.
options.C: minutes.

question: The term rules of order refers to the

options.B: agenda.
options.C: adopted bylaws.

question: Ordinary societies usually provide themselves with suitable rules of order by naming an edition of a parliamentary law manual in its bylaws. This manual is then called the organization's

options.B: resolutions for a parliamentary authority.
options.C: parliamentary authority.

question: Rules of order that supplement or modify the rules contained in an organization's parliamentary authority are called

options.B: special rules of order.
options.C: the secondary parliamentary authority.

question: In a mass meeting or a meeting of a body not yet organized, adopting a parliamentary authority

options.A: may take place at the beginning of the meeting.
options.B: must be included by the second meeting.
options.C: is not usually required by a society with less than one hundred members.
options.D: may take place at the close of the meeting.

question: If a special rule of order is not in agreement with an organization's parliamentary authority, which one must be used?

options.B: The special rule
options.C: It is decided by a majority vote of the assembly.
options.D: Neither one. The organization's secondary parliamentary authority would be consulted.

question: If an organization has adopted Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised as their parliamentary authority and another manual disagrees with a specific rule, which manual is binding?

options.A: The assembly votes and chooses the binding manual by a majority vote.
options.B: The parliamentarian decides which manual is binding.
options.C: Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised is binding.
options.D: The officers meet in executive session to decide which manual should be binding.

question: Special rules of order

options.A: should be adopted as part of the bylaws.
options.B: cannot be suspended.
options.C: should be adopted separately from the bylaws.
options.D: should be voted on by the officers before being proposed to the organization.

question: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to suspend rules of order named in an organization's parliamentary authority or adopted as special rules of order is

options.A: a majority of the entire membership and previous notice.
options.B: three-fourths of the members present and voting.
options.C: a fifth (20%) of the members voting.
options.D: two-thirds of the members present and voting.

question: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to adopt or amend special rules of order that are separate from the bylaws is

options.B: two-thirds without previous notice.
options.C: a majority of the entire membership with notice.
options.D: two-thirds with previous notice or a vote of a majority of the entire membership.

question: Standing rules

options.A: are always adopted at the same time a society is organized.
options.B: can be adopted by a 49% affirmative vote.
options.C: are related to the details of administration rather than parliamentary procedure.
options.D: must have previous notice to be adopted.

question: Ordinary standing rules generally contain

options.A: rules that may not be changed except with previous notice and a two-thirds vote.
options.B: the object and standing committees of the organization.
options.C: an hour that sets the time meetings are to begin.
options.D: rules of parliamentary procedure related to the presiding officer.

question: Which of the following is an example of a standing rule?

options.B: Defining a quorum for the organization
options.C: The maintenance of a guest register
options.D: Listing the duties of the chairman of all the Standing Committees

question: The minimum affirmative vote to adopt a standing rule at any business meeting is a

options.B: two-thirds without previous notice.
options.C: a majority without previous notice.
options.D: a majority and mandatory previous notice.

question: A standing rule remains in effect until

options.B: the end of the meeting.
options.C: the member who proposed the rule withdraws it.
options.D: the parliamentarian decides it has no value for the organization.

question: At a formal meeting, and without notice, a deliberative assembly has the right to temporarily suspend its

options.B: constitution or bylaws.
options.C: charter.

question: The quorum of an assembly is

options.A: two-thirds of the members present at a meeting.
options.B: the largest number that can be depended on to attend any meeting.
options.C: the minimum number of members who must be present for business to be legally transacted.
options.D: the number of members who always vote on motions brought before the assembly.

question: In the absence of a provision in the bylaws, the quorum of an organized society is

options.B: a majority of the entire membership.
options.C: a majority of the members who answer roll call.
options.D: two-thirds of its officers in attendance.

question: The minimum essential officers that must be present to conduct business in a deliberative assembly are a

options.B: presiding officer and a treasurer.
options.C: presiding officer and a secretary or clerk.

question: Which phrase below applies both to the presiding officer and to the station in the place where he/she presides?

options.B: "The podium"
options.C: "The moderator"

question: The president or chief officer of an organized society who normally presides at its meetings is addressed as

options.B: "Mr. or Madam President"
options.C: "Mr. or Madam Presiding Officer."
options.D: "Mr. or Madam President pro tem" or "Mr. or Madam Chairmember."

question: How should a vice-president be addressed while actually presiding if the president is not on the platform?

options.B: "Mr. or Madam President"
options.C: "Mr. or Madam Acting President"

question: With very few exceptions, a member never speaks

options.B: more than once on a main motion.
options.C: unless permission is granted by the maker of the motion.

question: During a regular meeting, the presiding officer refers to himself/herself as

options.B: "your presiding officer."
options.C: "the chair."

question: An appropriate phrase to use by the presiding officer to call a meeting to order is

options.B: "Order, please."
options.C: "Could I have your attention, please?"

question: What specifies the sequence in which certain general types or classes of business are brought up or permitted to be introduced at a meeting?

options.B: Bylaws
options.C: Standing rules

question: A society which has adopted Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised as its parliamentary authority

options.A: may use a new parliamentary authority at each meeting.
options.B: must follow the order of business given in the parliamentary manual.
options.C: may adopt its own particular order of business.
options.D: may change any item in the parliamentary authority by a majority vote without notice.

question: After the presiding officer calls a meeting to order, the next order of business is usually

options.B: reports of officers.
options.C: unfinished business.
options.D: reading and approval of the minutes.

question: In the standard order of business, the reports of officers are presented

options.B: immediately before new business.
options.C: immediately after approval of the minutes.

question: In the standard order of business, what follows special orders?

options.B: Standing committee reports
options.C: Unfinished business and general orders

question: In the standard order of business, new business is taken up

options.A: after unfinished business and general orders.
options.B: immediately after reports of officers.
options.C: at the discretion of the president.
options.D: whenever members wish to propose main motions.

question: A mass meeting usually does not need an order of business because

options.A: unfinished business is taken up first.
options.B: the chair determines the agenda by asking the officers to draft one after the meeting begins.
options.C: only new business can be brought up.
options.D: the committee that was assigned the problem for the meeting conducts a panel discussion.

question: Calling a meeting to order is

options.A: always completed after the minutes are read.
options.B: the first item of business.
options.C: not part of the order of business.

question: A convention commonly

options.A: uses the same order of business prescribed for regular quarterly meetings.
options.B: accepts and uses the order of business recommended by the officers.
options.C: adopts its own order of business.
options.D: does not follow an order of business.

question: Business is brought before an assembly by a member making a formal proposal called a (an)

options.B: motion.
options.C: order.

question: A communication addressed to the organization is normally read aloud at a meeting by the

options.B: vice-president.
options.C: committee chairman.

question: The reading of a communication at a meeting means that

options.A: a motion is not formally before the assembly.
options.B: the communication must be debated and voted on.
options.C: a committee should be appointed to investigate the communication.
options.D: the member who originally read the communication is the only one who may amend it.

question: The formal parliamentary name given to any form of discussion of the merits of a motion is called

options.B: an argument.
options.C: a debate.

question: The chair must recognize any

options.A: officer who seeks the floor, in preference to a member.
options.B: member who seeks the floor while entitled to it.
options.C: person in the assembly who seeks the floor.
options.D: member of the board in preference to any regular member.

question: Before members in a large assembly can debate or propose motions, they must

options.B: address the chairman.
options.C: raise a hand.

question: Before a member of an assembly is allowed to speak or propose a motion, he or she must "obtain the floor." This means that the member must

options.A: rise and come before the assembly before speaking.
options.B: obtain permission from the assembly before addressing the chairman and speaking.
options.C: rise, address the chair, and wait to be recognized before speaking.
options.D: address the chair and then speak.

question: When a member "has the floor," this means that

options.A: anyone else in the assembly may speak from their seat.
options.B: a main motion need not be seconded.
options.C: another member may also stand and make a motion.
options.D: recognition has been received from the chair.

question: The expression "privileges of the floor" means that

options.A: a person is permitted to enter the room in which a meeting is being held that is usually restricted by members or staff.
options.B: a member may debate motions as many times as desired.
options.C: certain members must be recognized and given the floor at any time.
options.D: anyone present at a meeting may have the floor.

question: A member addressing the chair to claim the floor when the names of the members are not known should

options.B: state his/her name and appropriate identifying information.
options.C: wait until the presiding officer asks his/her name.
options.D: wait until the secretary notifies the presiding officer of his/her name before speaking.

question: When a member yields the floor by sitting, this means that

options.A: any other member is allowed to speak immediately.
options.B: there is an immediate vote on the pending motion.
options.C: the member is finished speaking.
options.D: the member may name another member to debate.

question: Generally, if two members rise at about the same time, the chairman should recognize the member who

options.A: is an officer of the organization.
options.B: raised a hand and stood up.
options.C: has the most seniority.
options.D: rose and addressed the chair first after the floor was yielded.

question: If you were the presiding officer and several members addressed the chair at about the same time after a motion was made, you should call on the member who

options.B: has the same opinions as all the other previous speakers.
options.C: has debated once.
options.D: made the motion and has not debated.

question: If the chairman makes a mistake and calls on the wrong member, attention to correct the error can be called by a member immediately

options.B: raising a Point of Order.
options.C: raising a Question of Privilege.

question: A motion is brought before the assembly by a member

options.A: making a motion and the chairman stating it.
options.B: making a motion, another member seconding it, and the chair stating it.
options.C: proposing, seconding and debating a motion.
options.D: asking the chair to offer a specific topic open for debate and then taking an immediate vote.

question: After a motion is made, seconded, and restated by the chair, the motion is

options.B: "pending."
options.C: always amended.
options.D: "put" by the chair as the next step.

question: If an assembly decides to do what a motion proposes, the motion is carried or

options.B: accepted.
options.C: passed.

question: If an assembly decides not to do what a motion proposes, the motion is rejected or

options.B: failed.
options.C: lost.

question: Main motions should start with the words

options.B: "I so move . . ."
options.C: "I wish to move . . ."

question: Complex motions are presented in the form of a (an)

options.B: charter
options.C: secondary amendment.

question: The member who proposes a main motion has the right to speak in debate

options.B: first and last.
options.C: three different times.

question: After members make motions, they should

options.A: remain standing and wait for permission to debate.
options.B: resume their seats.
options.C: debate the motion.
options.D: sit and wait for another member to ask a question so that debate may proceed.

question: Before proposing a main motion, a member may

options.A: not offer an explanation for the motion or debate it.
options.B: offer an explanation of a few words.
options.C: explain all the reasons in detail for making the motion.
options.D: debate the motion up to ten minutes.

question: Members who are unsure of the proper wording of a motion

options.A: may ask another member to assist without permission of the assembly.
options.B: may seek assistance from the chairman.
options.C: must sit, have the business of the assembly stop, and propose the motion when they are ready with the proper wording.
options.D: will be directed by the chairman to confer with the secretary while the meeting continues.

question: The member who wishes to second a motion must

options.B: second the motion before it may be considered.
options.C: rise and be recognized by the chair before seconding it.
options.D: be acceptable to the member who proposed the motion.

question: The seconder of a motion

options.B: should always stand and give his/her name.
options.C: must be recognized by the chair.
options.D: does not need to obtain the floor.

question: After a main motion has been made, another member--without obtaining the floor and who wishes the motion to be considered--says

options.B: "I second it."
options.C: "Second."

question: Motions proposed in small boards or committees

options.B: may be seconded by the maker of the motion.
options.C: need not be seconded.
options.D: must be seconded by the presiding officer.

question: Assume that a main motion is not seconded. What should the chairman say?

options.B: Repeat the following three times: "Will some member please second the motion?"
options.C: "Since there is no second, the motion is not before this meeting."
options.D: "Since there is no second, will the maker of the motion withdraw it?"

question: A second implies that the seconder agrees that the motion

options.A: must be entered in the minutes.
options.B: should come before the assembly.
options.C: can be adopted without change.
options.D: could be referred to a committee after it is adopted.

question: May a member who is opposed to a motion second it?

options.B: No
options.C: Yes, if a reason is offered
options.D: Only if the chair allows it

question: The requirement of a second to a motion is for the guidance of the

options.A: maker of the motion to determine who supports the motion.
options.B: secretary in recording the name of the seconder in the minutes.
options.C: chair so that the question on the motion can be stated.
options.D: members to recognize who supports the motion.

question: The purpose of a second to a motion is to

options.A: establish the fact that at least two members are willing to speak in favor of the motion.
options.B: prevent time from being consumed by the assembly having to dispose of a motion that only one member wants introduced.
options.C: establish the fact that at least two members are willing to vote in favor of the motion.
options.D: indicate to the chairman that members must debate the motion before it is voted on.

question: If the chair is sure that over a majority of the assembly approves a motion,

options.A: amendments may also be included without a second.
options.B: a second is not needed, even if a point of order is made.
options.C: the question can be stated without a second.
options.D: a second still must be made.

question: If a motion is considered and adopted without having been seconded, it

options.B: must be proposed, seconded and voted on again at a future meeting.
options.C: is still adopted.
options.D: is automatically laid on the table.

question: After a motion is made and seconded, the chair states the question. This means that the chairman

options.A: asks members if they have questions about the motion.
options.B: repeats the exact motion and indicates it is open for debate.
options.C: asks if the member who proposed the motion wishes to change it.
options.D: directs at least two questions to the member who made the motion.

question: A debatable motion is placed on the floor and is opened for debate after the

options.A: member who seconded the motion speaks for it.
options.B: motion has been stated by the chair.
options.C: member makes the motion.

question: The statement by the chair, "Are you ready for the question?" means the

options.A: assembly may not debate the pending question.
options.B: assembly must decide if it is ready to ask questions.
options.C: members may debate the pending question.
options.D: members may ask the maker of the motion questions.

question: A proper statement by the chairman after a motion has been made and seconded is

options.B: "It is moved and seconded that . . ."
options.C: "The motion has been made and seconded that . . ."
options.D: "Is there debate on the motion that . . .?"

question: If a motion is made that cannot be debated or amended, the chair would

options.A: say, "Are you ready for the question?"
options.B: still ask if the maker of the motion wants to give reasons for proposing the motion.
options.C: put the motion to a vote immediately after stating it.
options.D: say, "Since this motion cannot be debated or amended, it is adopted."

question: When a member's motion is not in order, the chair says,

options.B: "I rule your motion is out of order because . . ."
options.C: "I'm sorry, Mary, you made a mistake and you are out of order because . . ."
options.D: "The chair rules that the motion is out of order because . . ."

question: Which one of the following statements is true?

options.A: A main motion must always be in writing when it comes from an ad hoc committee.
options.B: A motion should never be in writing.
options.C: The chair can require that a main motion be in writing.
options.D: The secretary can demand that a main motion should always be in writing.

question: The maker of a motion has the right to modify or withdraw it

options.B: up to adjournment of the meeting.
options.C: until the chair states the question.

question: The seconder of a motion has the right to withdraw his/her second

options.B: if the maker of the motion modifies the motion that was seconded before it is stated by the chair.
options.C: immediately after the motion is stated by the chair.
options.D: after the minutes are read for approval by the assembly.

question: What is the proper order of steps in considering a main motion?

options.A: Members debate, the chair puts the question, and the chair announces the voting results.
options.B: The chair puts the question, members debate, the chair announces the results of the voting.
options.C: The chair puts the question, the chair announces the results of the voting, and members debate.
options.D: Members debate, the chair announces the voting results, and the chair puts the question.

question: Immediately after stating the question, the chair should turn toward the maker of the motion to see if he or she

options.A: wants to recommend a member to second the motion.
options.B: wishes the motion to be repeated.
options.C: wishes to be assigned the floor to debate.
options.D: wants the assembly to debate the motions immediately without debate.

question: The maker of a motion

options.A: must always speak first in debate on the motion.
options.B: may assign his/her right to debate to another member without permission of the assembly.
options.C: has the right to speak first and last on his or her motion.
options.D: has the right to speak first in debate on the motion.

question: Unless there is a rule to the contrary, a member may speak

options.B: twice during the same day.
options.C: three times on the same motion on the same day.
options.D: twice on the same motion on the same day.

question: How long can a member speak each time on a pending motion unless permission is given by the assembly or it is outlined differently in the bylaws?

options.B: Five minutes
options.C: Two minutes

question: Debate on a question must be confined to

options.A: affirmative points on the pending question.
options.B: the merits of the immediately pending question.
options.C: remarks and questions directed to the maker of the motion.
options.D: arguments that would promote the question not to be adopted.

question: Which rule of debate listed below is false?

options.A: Personal comments should not be interjected by the chairman.
options.B: The chair should not enter into debate while presiding.
options.C: The chairman cannot arbitrarily close debate.
options.D: The chair can interrupt the speaker for any reason.

question: A motion is recorded in the minutes

options.A: as the wording was improved by the secretary after the meeting.
options.B: as it was stated by the maker.
options.C: as it was stated by the chair just before being voted on by the assembly.
options.D: after the secretary changes the motion to make certain it satisfies the needs of the organization.

question: When the presiding officer puts the question, this means that the chair

options.B: proceeds to take a vote on the pending motion.
options.C: is going to ask the maker of the motion a question.
options.D: is going to put the pending motion on temporary hold.

question: The initial vote on a main motion is usually taken "viva voce," which means by

options.B: a show of hands.
options.C: voice.

question: Which vote on a motion is always taken first by the presiding officer?

options.B: Negative
options.C: Abstentions

question: If the affirmative vote is almost unanimous on a motion that is complimentary and noncontroversial, the chairman

options.A: need not call for a negative vote.
options.B: calls for a standing vote to confirm it.
options.C: takes only the negative vote by a division.
options.D: doesn't need to call for a negative vote even if a member objects.

question: When the chairman takes a vote on a motion, the abstentions are

options.B: called for last and used to calculate the majority number.
options.C: not taken.

options.D: Ask for more debate on the amendment.

question: The motion to Lay on the Table enables an assembly to lay a pending question aside

options.A: temporarily when something else of immediate urgency has arisen.
options.B: to consider any motion decided upon by the chairman.
options.C: so that the assembly may conduct a standing vote.
options.D: so that it can be brought up as a general order at the next meeting.

question: The motion to Lay on the Table

options.A: can be debated if the chairman allows the maker of the motion to speak first.
options.B: kills the motion and avoids a direct vote on it.
options.C: can be amended.
options.D: sets the pending question aside temporarily and there is no set time for taking up the matter again.

question: The motion to Lay on the Table is commonly misused in meetings in the place of the motion to

options.B: Postpone to a Certain Time.
options.C: Reconsider.

category: How a Group Can Change Its Mind

question: If a member proposed the motion to Lay on the Table and specifies a time for resuming consideration, what would you do as chairman?

options.A: Ask for a second and conduct a vote on it.
options.B: Handle it as two separate motions.
options.C: Suggest that the maker of the motion submit it as a Motion to Postpone.
options.D: Rule the motion out of order.

question: A subsidiary motion to Lay on the Table takes precedence over

options.A: the motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn.
options.B: all privileged motions.
options.C: all other subsidiary motions.

question: The motion to Lay on the Table is a motion that can be

options.B: applied to the motion to Limit Debate.
options.C: made when the Previous Question has been made.

question: If a main motion and a primary amendment are pending, and a motion to lay the main motion on the table is adopted, the amendment itself

options.A: can be brought up by any member as a new motion.
options.B: becomes the immediately pending question.
options.C: dies and is taken up under unfinished business at the next regular meeting.
options.D: adheres to the main motion and goes to the table with it.

question: Which one of the following subsidiary motions can be applied to the motion to Lay on the Table?

options.B: Refer to a Committee
options.C: Previous Question
options.D: None of the above. No subsidiary motion can be applied to the motion to Lay on the Table.

question: The motion to Lay on the Table is out of order when

options.A: both a main motion and an amendment are pending.
options.B: another member has the floor.
options.C: a motion has been adopted to extend the limits of debate.
options.D: there is another subsidiary motion pending.

question: Which statement below is true regarding the subsidiary motion To Lay on the Table?

options.B: The maker of the motion may state the reason prior to proposing the motion.
options.C: All amendments to the motion must pass by a majority vote.
options.D: The chair should not ask the maker of the motion to state the reason first.

question: On which one of the following subsidiary motions can only the negative vote sometimes be reconsidered?

options.B: Postpone to a Certain Time
options.C: Lay on the Table

question: One of the rules related to the motion to Take From the Table is that it

options.A: must be made by the same member who proposed the tabled motion.
options.B: can be proposed during the interrupting business.
options.C: can be proposed during any pending business.
options.D: requires a majority vote for its adoption.

category: How a Group Can Change Its Mind

question: In organizations that hold regular business sessions as often as quarterly, a question laid on the table remains there until taken from the table or until the end of the

options.B: next regular session.
options.C: next special meeting.

category: How a Group Can Change Its Mind

question: It is out of order to move to lay a pending question on the table if

options.A: the motion on the previous question is pending.
options.B: the motion to be laid on the table has an amendment already applied to it.
options.C: another member has already moved to lay the matter on the table during the same meeting.
options.D: there is evidently no other matter urgently requiring immediate attention.

question: Assume that a main motion is being debated and you become aware that something else of immediate urgency has arisen. What should you do?

options.A: Obtain the floor and say, "I move to lay the question on the table."
options.B: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I move to postpone the motion."
options.C: Obtain the floor and say, "I move to lay the question on the table until 10:00 a.m."
options.D: From your seat, and without obtaining the floor say, "I move to postpone the motion indefinitely until after we decide the urgent matter of . . ."

question: The privileged motion to Call for the Orders of the Day is used primarily to

options.A: order the chairman to take an immediate recess.
options.B: require that a meeting conform to its agenda.
options.C: indicate to members when a point of order may be called.
options.D: write orders for all committees to complete their tasks by a specific time.

question: The orders of the day can be called by

options.A: one member proposing the motion and a second.
options.B: a two-thirds vote without notice.
options.C: any member.
options.D: the officers after they confer in executive session and adopt it by a two-thirds vote.

question: The privileged motion to Call for the Orders of the Day may not be

options.B: debated.
options.C: amended.

question: The orders of the day can be set aside by

options.B: any member who objects.
options.C: the chairman if there is an important item being debated.

category: How a Group Can Change Its Mind

question: Assume you are chairman at a meeting. The orders of the day are called for, and you sense that the assembly would prefer to consider the pending question. What would be the proper procedure?

options.A: Proceed with fulfilling the request for the orders of the day.
options.B: The chair could call for a vote on whether the assembly wishes to consider the orders of the day.
options.C: Ignore the request and proceed with the pending question.
options.D: Call the member who called for the orders of the day out of order.

question: Once an assembly has refused to proceed to the orders of the day, the orders of the day cannot be called for again until the pending business

options.A: has been debated by at least one member in favor and one member opposed to it.
options.B: has been amended.
options.C: is adopted.

question: Assume that there is a meeting in progress and the assembly has digressed from the agenda to such an extent that the important items on the agenda may not be considered because of a lack of time. What would you do?

options.A: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "Madam President, I order you to consider the agenda."
options.B: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "Madam President, I move we reconsider the agenda."
options.C: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "Madam President, I call for the orders of the day."
options.D: Obtain the floor and say, "I move that we order the consideration of our agenda."

category: How a Group Can Change Its Mind

question: The motion to Raise a Question of Privilege is a device which

options.A: is ruled upon by the chair, and the ruling can be reconsidered.
options.B: has a higher precedence than any incidental motion.
options.C: requires a second and is debatable.
options.D: may permit action otherwise not in order.

question: Raising a question of privilege while business is pending

options.A: cannot usually interrupt a member speaking.
options.B: requires recognition from the chairman to state the request.
options.C: cannot be made while an amendment is pending.
options.D: requires a two-thirds vote in order to be adopted.

question: The motion to Raise a Question of Privilege takes precedence over all the motions below except the motion to

options.B: Commit (or Refer).
options.C: Limit Debate.

question: A member who has been assigned the floor may be interrupted for the purpose of

options.B: limiting debate.
options.C: raising a question of privilege.

question: The privileged device, Raise a Question of Privilege, is not

options.B: debatable.
options.C: seconded.

question: Who makes the initial ruling on the motion to Raise a Question of Privilege?

options.B: The chairman
options.C: The parliamentarian

question: MEMBER:-(Rising, and without obtaining the floor) "I rise to a question of privilege affecting the assembly." The statement above can be used by a member at a meeting to

options.A: demand an immediate vote on the pending question.
options.B: request a standing, counted vote on an amendment.
options.C: ask another member a question related to a privileged motion.
options.D: request that specific windows be opened to increase the ventilation in the meeting room.

question: Which one of the following would not be a topic to justify a member making a Question of Privilege effecting the assembly?

options.B: Charges circulated against a member's character
options.C: A motion to go into executive session

question: If a motion is made as a question of privilege and it is seconded, what would you do as chairman?

options.B: Call the motion out of order.
options.C: Call for debate, and then vote on it.
options.D: Take an immediate vote on it.

question: Assume that the meeting hall is very noisy because of the construction of a new road next to the building. What motion could you propose before asking the chairman to try to solve the problem?

options.A: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I rise to a point of order."
options.B: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "Mr. President, I rise to a question of privilege affecting the assembly."
options.C: Obtain the floor and say, "Mr. President, I rise to a point of information regarding the noise coming from outside our meeting hall."
options.D: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "Mr. President, I cannot hear you speaking and move that you turn up the volume on the public address system."

question: At a regular meeting, a controversial matter that demands immediate action is introduced as a main motion. During debate, a member interrupts, rises to a question of privilege, and moves "that the meeting be closed and that nonmembers be asked to leave." What would you do as chairman?

options.A: Declare the motion out of order.
options.B: Put the motion to an immediate vote.
options.C: Ask for a second and debate on the new motion.

question: A Recess may be taken to

options.B: secure information.
options.C: allow for informal consultation.

question: When a motion to Recess is made while another motion is pending it is a (an)

options.B: privileged motion.
options.C: incidental main motion.

question: The privileged motion to Recess is a motion that a recess begin

options.A: after the motion on the floor is disposed of.
options.B: immediately.
options.C: when the member who proposed the pending motion grants permission.
options.D: upon a decision of the chair.

question: A motion to recess that is made when no business is pending is a

options.B: main motion.
options.C: incidental motion.

question: Which of the following is true of the privileged motion to recess?

options.A: It may provide for a recess at a later time.
options.B: It requires that the duration of the recess be included in the motion.
options.C: The vote may be reconsidered.
options.D: It is "privileged" only when it is proposed while another question is pending.

question: Assume a main motion is pending at a regular meeting. A member gains the floor and moves that the assembly recess for dinner after the vote on the pending motion. What would you do as chairman?

options.A: Declare the motion to recess out of order.
options.B: Take a voice vote on the motion to recess without a second.
options.C: Call for a second on the motion to recess and then take an immediate voice vote.

question: The motion to take a Recess at a future time may be proposed only

options.B: if the member who made the immediately pending motion agrees.
options.C: when another question is pending.
options.D: during the time before new business will be considered.

question: The privileged motion to Recess has precedence over the motion to

options.A: Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn.
options.B: Adjourn.
options.C: Refer to a Committee.

question: The privileged motion to Recess

options.A: requires a two-thirds vote to be adopted.
options.B: is amendable as to the length of the recess.
options.C: is debatable.

question: An amendment to the privileged motion to Recess

options.A: must relate to which members may take the recess.
options.B: is never allowed.
options.C: is not debatable.
options.D: requires a two-thirds vote to be adopted.

question: How does the chair handle a recess if it is provided for in an adopted agenda?

options.A: The chair requests that a member make a motion to have a recess.
options.B: The chair appoints a committee to determine the proper procedure for announcing the recess.
options.C: The chair declares the recess at the specified time.
options.D: A member calls for the order of the day, it is seconded, and the chair conducts a voice vote.

question: If a prescheduled recess is not announced by the chair at the scheduled time, a member should

options.A: rise to a point of order.
options.B: move that a recess be taken.
options.C: call for the orders of the day.
options.D: rise and make an amendment of the recess time on the pending amendment.

question: The time for taking a pre-scheduled recess can be postponed by a

options.A: two-thirds vote of the people attending.
options.B: two-thirds vote of the assembly.
options.C: majority vote of the quorum.

question: Assume that your organization is debating a motion and you want to talk privately to several fellow members about the business at hand. What would you do?

options.A: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I move we postpone the motion for ten minutes and take a recess."
options.B: From your seat, and without obtaining the floor yell out, "Recess!"
options.C: Obtain the floor and say, "I move we lay the motion on the table and take a ten minute recess."
options.D: Obtain the floor and say, "I move to recess for ten minutes."

question: The gavel may be rapped to signal

options.A: a recess, an adjournment, and a breach of order.
options.B: when a motion has been adopted, a division, and a point of information.
options.C: a question of privilege, the adoption of an amendment, and the start of debate on main motions.
options.D: when the chairman has cast the deciding vote on any motion.

question: Which one of the following would be an example of the privileged motion to Adjourn?

options.A: Obtain the floor and say, "I move that we adjourn at 7:30 p.m."
options.B: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I move that we adjourn sine die."
options.C: Obtain the floor and say, "I move to adjourn."
options.D: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I move that we now adjourn to meet at 7:30 p.m. on May 15th."

question: The privileged motion to Adjourn is

options.A: always moved in an unqualified form.
options.B: a motion to close the meeting immediately.
options.C: made when no time for adjourning has been set.

question: A motion to Adjourn is always privileged when

options.A: the time for adjournment has been set ahead of time.
options.B: it sets a time to adjourn (is qualified).
options.C: no time for adjournment has been set (is unqualified).

question: If a motion to adjourn is qualified in any way (example: "I move we adjourn in ten minutes"), it is classified as a (an)

options.B: privileged motion.
options.C: subsidiary motion.

question: A motion to Adjourn at or to a future time while business is pending

options.A: may be adopted anytime during a recess, without a quorum.
options.B: should be completed prior to debate on the pending motion.
options.C: is permissible if the chair allows it.

question: The motion to Adjourn is always

options.B: applied to other motions.
options.C: a privileged motion when not qualified.
options.D: in order when another member has the floor.

question: The privileged motion to Adjourn takes precedence over all motions except the motion to

options.A: Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn.
options.B: Recess.
options.C: Amend.

question: When the privileged motion to Adjourn is pending, which motion below is in order?

options.B: Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn
options.C: Call for the Orders of the Day

question: The privileged motion to Adjourn

options.A: may be proposed when another member has the floor.
options.B: is amendable.
options.C: must be seconded.

question: If a motion to Adjourn is defeated, who may move to reconsider the vote?

options.A: Any member who is recognized by the chair
options.B: Any member who voted on the negative side
options.C: Any member who voted on the affirmative side

category: How a Group Can Change Its Mind

question: If a question is pending at an organized monthly meeting and an adjournment closed the meeting, the pending motion

options.A: is taken up as the first item under unfinished business at the next monthly meeting.
options.B: must be introduced again at the next meeting in order to be considered.
options.C: is laid on the table.

question: A motion to close the session of an assembly and dissolve it is referred to as a motion to "adjourn sine die," which means to

options.A: "take a short recess prior to final adjournment."
options.B: "adjourn and declare that the organization no longer exists."
options.C: "adjourn without day."

question: While the privileged motion to Adjourn is pending, it is not in order to

options.B: make a main motion.
options.C: give notice of a motion to be made at the next meeting.
options.D: make a motion to Reconsider and Enter in the Minutes.

category: How a Group Can Change Its Mind

question: If the privileged motion to Adjourn is voted down, the motion can be renewed

options.A: only after debate on the adjournment occurs.
options.B: after additional debate occurs.
options.C: only after action on the pending main motion is completed.

question: A motion to adjourn that has obviously been made for obstructive purposes should be

options.A: refused to be entertained by the chairman.
options.B: voted on immediately.
options.C: stated by the chair after a second.
options.D: referred to the assembly by the chair for debate.

question: If it appears that there is no further business in a meeting of an ordinary society, the chair should state

options.A: "All those in favor of adjourning, say 'Aye.' Those opposed, say 'No.'"
options.B: "The meeting is adjourned."
options.C: "Is there any further business? Since there is no further business, the meeting is adjourned."

question: Which of the following is the correct form to use in making the motion to adjourn as a main motion?

options.B: "I move that we now adjourn to meet at 6 p.m. on May 5."
options.C: "I move that the meeting adjourn."

question: Assume that it is 11:00 p.m. and there has been prolonged debate on the last, unimportant agenda item. You want the meeting to end. What should you do?

options.A: From your seat, and without obtaining the floor say, "I move to adjourn."
options.B: Obtain the floor and say, "I move to adjourn."
options.C: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I move to adjourn."

question: The purpose of the privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn is to establish a (an)

options.B: annual meeting.
options.C: regular meeting.

question: Which motion below has the effect of setting the time, and sometimes the place, for another meeting to continue the business of the meeting?

options.B: Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn
options.C: Recess
options.D: Call for the Orders of the Day

question: The motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn is a privileged motion only if it is made

options.A: when a member rises to a Question of Privilege and makes a motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn.
options.B: if no question is pending.
options.C: and the maker of the immediately pending motion agrees to have it considered.

question: Depending on the circumstances, the motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn may be proposed as a privileged motion or a (an)

options.B: subsidiary motion.
options.C: main motion (incidental main motion).

question: If a motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn is made when no question is pending,

options.A: the chairman should rule it out of order.
options.B: it should be voted on immediately after a second.
options.C: it is subject to all the rules applicable to a main motion.
options.D: a two-thirds vote is necessary for its adoption.

question: Which statement below is false regarding the privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn?

options.A: It affects the time when the present meeting will adjourn.
options.B: An amendment may be applied to it.
options.C: It is out of order when another member has the floor.

question: The privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn

options.A: may be applied to any motion.
options.B: is not debatable
options.C: does not require a second.
options.D: cannot be amended as to the date.

question: MEMBER:-(After obtaining the floor) "I move that when this meeting adjourns, it adjourn to meet at 9 a.m. next Wednesday." The adoption of this motion establishes a (an)

options.B: adjourned meeting.
options.C: recessed meeting.

question: The effect of adopting the privileged motion to Fix the Time to Which to Adjourn is to

options.B: recess immediately.
options.C: establish a continuation of the present meeting.
options.D: set a time for adjourning the next meeting.

question: Assume that the assembly is debating a main motion and the hour is getting late. You want to make sure that the assembly meets again tomorrow to complete the agenda. What could you do?

options.A: Obtain the floor and say, "I move we table the remaining agenda and adjourn until tomorrow."
options.B: Obtain the floor and say, "I move we recess until tomorrow at 9:00 a.m."
options.C: Obtain the floor and say, "I move that when this meeting adjourns, it adjourns to meet again at 9:00 a.m. tomorrow."
options.D: Obtain the floor and say, "I move we adjourn."

question: Which motion below could be made so that the chair would be called on to enforce a violated rule?

options.B: Point of Order
options.C: Suspend the Rules

question: A Point of Order yields to all

options.B: secondary motions.
options.C: subsidiary motions.

question: If a Point of Order is raised while an amendment is immediately pending, the

options.B: amendment is disposed of first, and the point of order next.
options.C: point of order is disposed of first.
options.D: chair asks for a second on the point of order and then it is ruled on.

question: After a member makes a Point of Order, the chair should always

options.B: determine if the maker wishes to debate it first.
options.C: make certain that amendments that are applied to it are germane.
options.D: try to make a ruling on it.

question: When a member makes a Point of Order, how is it normally decided?

options.B: It can be adopted by a majority vote of the assembly.
options.C: It can be adopted by a two-thirds vote of the assembly after it is seconded.
options.D: The parliamentarian rises after the breach of order is described by the member and immediately rules on it.

question: The normal grounds for a member to rise to a Point of Order are

options.A: to ask the maker of the motion a question.
options.B: uncomfortable conditions in the meeting room.
options.C: a breach of rules.
options.D: to obtain parliamentary information from the parliamentarian.

question: Which motion below would be proper to use if the presiding officer at your organization's meeting asked for debate on a main motion before it was seconded?

options.B: Point of Order
options.C: Question of Privilege

question: Which statement below is true regarding a Point of Order?

options.A: Points of order should be called on minor irregularities.
options.B: A parliamentary inquiry has the same purpose as a point of order.
options.C: If a motion is not seconded, and is debated and then adopted, a point of order is too late.
options.D: A member must rise and be recognized by the chair before raising a point of order.

question: Which motion below may be made if a member wants a speaker to conclude debate and is unsure that this member has breached a rule?

options.B: Parliamentary Inquiry
options.C: Reserve a Point of Order

question: Assume that a member at a meeting is debating the main motion while an amendment is the immediately pending question. What could you do to stop the member from speaking on the main motion?

options.A: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I rise to a point of order."
options.B: From your seat, and without obtaining the floor say, "Point of information."
options.C: Obtain the floor and say, "I rise to a question of privilege."
options.D: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I rise to a parliamentary inquiry."

question: If you were chairman and were unsure on how to rule on a Point of Order, what would you do?

options.A: Ignore it and make a ruling after the meeting and include it in the minutes.
options.B: Submit it to a vote of the assembly.
options.C: Notify the assembly that a ruling would be made after they debate the point of order.
options.D: Consult with all the officers immediately and then make a ruling.

question: An appeal from the decision of the chair is a

options.A: point of order stated in another way.
options.B: disagreement with the ruling of the chair.
options.C: demand to adhere to the agenda.
options.D: disagreement between members of the assembly.

question: A characteristic of the motion to Appeal is that it

options.A: takes two members to Appeal a chair's decision.
options.B: yields to all privileged motions.
options.C: yields to the Previous Question.

question: The incidental motion to Appeal is used

options.A: to have the chairman's ruling voted on by the assembly.
options.B: if a member wishes to appeal to the maker of a motion to accept an amendment.
options.C: when an accurate standing vote is needed on a main motion.
options.D: to point out that another member's debate is not germane.

question: The chair's ruling can be appealed

options.B: at the time of the ruling.
options.C: after the motion to adjourn has been seconded.
options.D: before the time of the ruling.

question: The incidental motion to Appeal

options.B: must be seconded.
options.C: may be amended.

question: The incidental motion to Appeal is debatable unless it

options.A: is made while the immediate pending question is undebatable.
options.B: relates to indecorum or a transgression of the rules of speaking.
options.C: relates to priority of business.

question: When the incidental motion to Appeal is debatable, no member can speak more than once except the

options.B: member who seconded the Appeal.
options.C: presiding officer, who may speak twice.

question: A tie vote on the motion to Appeal from the decision of the chair

options.A: sustains the decision of the chair.
options.B: means that the decision of the chair is not sustained.
options.C: automatically means a division of the assembly will be taken.
options.D: means that more debate will be allowed.

question: Which of the following would not be subject to an Appeal?

options.A: The chair's response to a parliamentary inquiry
options.B: The chair's announcement of the results of a vote
options.C: The chair's response to a point of information

question: Assume you are chairman and a member appeals your announcement of the results of a vote. What would you do?

options.B: Suggest that the member should call for a Division.
options.C: Take another voice vote.
options.D: Take a vote on the appeal.

question: Assume you do not agree with the chairman's ruling on your Point of Order. What could you do?

options.A: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I rise to a point of order over the decision of the chair."
options.B: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I rise to debate the chair on his ruling."
options.C: From your seat, and without obtaining the floor say, "I move the previous question."
options.D: Rise, and without obtaining the floor say, "I appeal from the decision of the chair."

question: The proper language to use by the chair for putting the affirmative vote of the question on an appeal is

options.A: "all those in favor of sustaining the chair, say 'aye.'"
options.B: "all those in favor of the chair, say 'aye.'"
options.C: "those in favor of sustaining the chair's decision, say 'aye.'"
options.D: "all those in favor of my decision, say 'aye.'"

question: When a member wishes to do something at a meeting that he/she cannot do without violating one or more of its regular rules, the assembly can adopt a motion to

options.A: appeal the decision of the chairman.
options.B: raise a question of privilege.
options.C: suspend the rules.
options.D: allow the chairman to change the rule without notice.

question: The incidental motion to Suspend the Rules

options.B: is debatable.
options.C: is amendable as to which rule is to be suspended.
options.D: may interrupt another member who has the floor.

question: The object of the incidental motion to Suspend the Rules is to suspend one or more rules contained in the

options.B: special rules of order.
options.C: standing rules of the assembly.

question: In making the motion to Suspend the Rules, the motion must

options.B: be made by the parliamentarian after conferring with the officers.
options.C: be adopted by unanimous consent.
options.D: be proposed before the rules of order have been adopted.

question: Rules that cannot generally be suspended are those that

options.B: protect the basic rights of individual members.
options.C: are in the bylaws (or constitution).

question: Which motion below would be used to dispense with the regular order of business and proceed to a subject that is scheduled later in the meeting?

options.B: Suspend the Rules
options.C: Reconsider the Order of Business

category: How a Group Can Change Its Mind

question: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to suspend rules of parliamentary procedure that are in an established parliamentary procedure manual is

options.B: two-thirds.
options.C: more than one-third.

question: Which of the following cannot be suspended by a majority vote?

options.A: A parliamentary rule adopted by the society as a rule of order.
options.B: A rule requiring previous notice for an amendment.
options.C: An established order of business previously adopted by the society.

category: How a Group Can Change Its Mind

question: The minimum affirmative vote necessary to suspend Standing Rules is

options.B: a majority without notice.
options.C: two-thirds without notice.

question: Which motion below would you make if an original main motion is proposed that is strongly undesirable?

question: Which of the following is the primary difference between a board and a committee?
