options.C: The board meets more frequently.
options.D: The quorum for a board is always larger.

question: When a committee is appointed "with power," this means that the committee has permission from the assembly to

options.A: conduct a regular meeting with the entire assembly and propose motions.
options.B: take action for all pending special committees.
options.C: take all the necessary steps to carry out its instructions.
options.D: require that the president of the society be the chairman of the committee.

question: A committee that has a continuing existence and is in the society's bylaws is called a (an)

options.B: standing committee.
options.C: ordinary committee.

question: If certain standing committees are listed in the bylaws, no other standing committees can be established unless the

options.B: bylaws are amended.
options.C: assembly allows it through the recommendation of an ad hoc committee.
options.D: entire organization is notified to ask for volunteers to serve on the new committee.

question: A standing committee of an organization reports to the

options.B: president.
options.C: assembly.

question: A committee that is appointed to carry out a specific task and ceases to exist when it has made a final report to the assembly may be called a (an)

options.B: select committee.
options.C: ad hoc committee.

question: After a "special committee" has made its final report to the assembly, it

options.A: is listed in the bylaws as a standing committee.
options.B: automatically ceases to exist.
options.C: is assigned new members and handles all related topics in the future.
options.D: cannot be discharged by the assembly.

question: The usual method of appointing assembly members to a special committee is

options.B: to select a committee chairman who then chooses the committee members.
options.C: by open nominations from the floor.
options.D: is specified in the motion that establishes the committee.

question: A vacancy occurring in a committee is filled by the

options.B: appointing power.
options.C: society.

question: If a standing committee has extensive powers, it is usually chosen in an election by

options.B: ballot.
options.C: rising.

question: Which of the following is a method of appointing committee members?

options.B: Nominations from the floor with a viva voce election
options.C: Nominations by the chairman

question: In large assemblies, special committees are generally appointed by the

options.B: secretary.
options.C: vice-president.

question: Some society's bylaws state that the president "shall appoint all committees." Which statement is false regarding this statement?

options.A: The president selects persons to serve on committees.
options.B: A committee cannot be created by the president.
options.C: No vote is generally taken on members who are appointed to a committee by the president.
options.D: None of the above. They are all true.

question: In general practice, when a committee is appointed by the president, the committee chairman is the

options.A: first member the chair names to the committee.
options.B: second member that the chair names to the committee.
options.C: last member named by the chair to the committee.
options.D: None of the above. The chair usually does not have the authority to name committee chairman.

question: A standing committee can appoint subcommittees whichj are then responsible to and report to the

options.B: standing committee.
options.C: chairman of the standing committee.

question: Which of the following is the duty of the secretary of a society when a committee is appointed?

options.A: Notify all persons who are appointed
options.B: Furnish a list of all members to the committee chairman
options.C: Provide copies of all papers, motions, or matters referred to it

question: What is the minimum number of committee members that can call a meeting if the chairman does not?

options.B: Three
options.C: Four
options.D: None of the above. Only the committee chairman can call a meeting.

question: If an assembly has no bylaw provision or rule about the quorum of a committee, what is the quorum of a standing committee?

options.A: All the members of the committee
options.B: The chairman and one other member
options.C: A majority of the committee members
options.D: Any number present at a properly called committee meeting

question: A quorum in a committee is

options.A: a majority of its membership unless the assembly has prescribed something different.
options.B: two-thirds of the entire membership of the committee.
options.C: three-fourths of the officers appointed by the chairman.
options.D: None of the above. There is no set quorum if not prescribed in the bylaws.

question: In relatively small standing and special committees, the chairman

options.B: may debate motions.
options.C: must rise when putting questions to a vote.
options.D: must enforce the rule that members may only debate twice on motions.

question: Committees of organized societies normally operate

options.A: with no rules of parliamentary procedure.
options.B: under the rules adopted by the chairman of the committee.
options.C: under the parliamentary authority adopted by the society.
options.D: with strict, formal parliamentary procedure rules, especially if the committee is under six members.

question: When members of a society appear before a committee to present their views on a subject studied by the committee, the meeting is called a

options.B: special committee report.
options.C: hearing.

question: When a special committee has completed the business it was assigned, a motion can be made for the committee to "rise," which means that the committee is

options.B: taking a rising vote on their recommendation.
options.C: being recognized for the work that they have accomplished.

question: Members of standing committees generally continue their duties until

options.B: the committee chairman excuses the committee permanently.
options.C: new officers of the society replace them.
options.D: their recommendations are put into effect.

question: The form for a detailed report by a committee should consist of four parts. Which part is covered last?

options.A: The facts uncovered or information obtained
options.B: Recommendations
options.C: A description of the way the committee undertook its charge
options.D: The findings or conclusions derived from the facts or information

question: Who is allowed to make a report for a board if the chairman of the board is also the presiding officer?

options.B: Any other member of the committee
options.C: The secretary of the committee

question: When an assembly receives a committee report, the assembly

options.A: has ratified the report subject to approval of the committee.
options.B: reviews the written report after hearing it.
options.C: hears the report that is read.
options.D: automatically reconsiders the report if it is adopted.

question: A committee report is read which contains certain recommendations. The appropriate motion at the end of the report made by the reporting committee member would be to

options.B: adopt the report.
options.C: implement the recommendations.

question: A motion made to the assembly after a committee report

options.B: has a higher precedence than the motion to amend.
options.C: requires no second.
options.D: can be proposed when another member is speaking.

question: A motion "to adopt the report" of a committee

options.B: has the effect of endorsing every word of the report.
options.C: should be made by the reporting member.

question: If a motion "to accept" a committee report is adopted, it implies that the assembly has

options.B: endorsed the entire report.
options.C: heard the report and agrees to part of it after an appropriate amendment.
options.D: agreed to hear the report and vote on it.

question: Which of the following is false regarding committee reports?

options.A: A written report is usually not addressed or dated.
options.B: The report should begin with the identification of the committee that submitted it.
options.C: The report generally should always be written in the first person.
options.D: The report should be submitted in writing.

question: An acceptable way to begin a standing committee report is to start with the words

options.B: "Mr. Jones' report . . . "
options.C: "We recommend . . . "

question: What should be written after the signature of the chairman if a committee authorizes its chairman to sign a report?

options.B: "Approved by all the committee members"
options.C: "Chairman"

question: If the order of business does not make a provision for a committee report that one member does not want to be received, and a member still wishes to make the report, what would you do as chairman?

options.A: Direct the member to proceed, even though some members object.
options.B: Deny the request.
options.C: Call the member out of order and order it placed on the agenda of the next regular meeting.
options.D: Put the question to the assembly.

question: After a report from a standing committee concludes by making a recommendation to adopt a resolution, how is the resolution adopted by the assembly?

options.A: The chairman takes an immediate vote on the resolution without a formal motion.
options.B: The resolution is adopted without a vote.
options.C: The reporting member proposes a motion.
options.D: It can't be adopted until the assembly discharges the committee.

question: How should the chair take a vote on a committee's recommendation of several amendments that will be debated?

options.A: Vote on the recommendations all at once after they are all read.
options.B: Take a vote on each recommendation after it is read and opened for debate.
options.C: Have the committee excused and vote for the entire assembly.
options.D: A vote is not required, since the committee recommended them for adoption.

question: The principal committees that perform parliamentary functions in the organization of a convention are the

options.A: Registration Committee and the Credential Committee.
options.B: Credentials Committee, the Committee on Standing Rules, and the Program Committee.
options.C: Bylaws Committee and the Committee on Standing Rules.
options.D: Credentials Committee, the Bylaws Committee, and the Committee on Standing Rules.

question: The formal presentation of the views of committee members who do not agree with the committee report is called a

options.B: "privileged report."
options.C: "minority report."

question: The report adopted by a majority in a committee is referred to as

options.B: "the majority report."
options.C: "the opinion of the majority."

question: The formal presentation of a "minority report"

options.A: must be presented before the committee report.
options.B: is always allowed without permission of the assembly.
options.C: is a privilege that the assembly may grant.
options.D: may be granted by the chairman without consulting the assembly.

question: If the minority committee report concludes with a proposed resolution, the minority can recommend

options.B: rejection of the resolution.
options.C: adoption of some other suitable motion.

question: If you were the chair and called for a minority report and a member of the assembly objects, what would you do?

options.A: Have the assembly vote on the request.
options.B: Have the assembly debate whether they wanted to hear the report and then vote on it.
options.C: Ignore the objection and allow the report.

question: The committee of the whole, quasi committee of the whole, and informal consideration all allow members to debate any main motion or amendment

options.B: twice.
options.C: as often as they can obtain the floor.

question: In which of the following types of committees would the president of a society normally act as the chairman?

options.B: Quasi Committee of the Whole
options.C: Committee of the Whole
options.D: Any Standing Committee without a permanent chairman

question: Which of the following is suited for large assemblies?

options.B: Quasi committee of the whole
options.C: Informal consideration

question: Which statement is true regarding a committee of the whole?

options.A: Members can debate one time on all main motions.
options.B: The results of votes taken are final assembly decisions.
options.C: The regular presiding officer is chairman.

question: The president normally acts as chairman for a

options.B: committee of the whole.
options.C: quasi committee of the whole.
options.D: committee that does not have a permanent chairman.

question: Which statement is true regarding the quasi committee of the whole?

options.A: Members can only debate motions three times.
options.B: The results of votes are final decisions of the assembly.
options.C: It is suited for groups of fifty to one-hundred members.
options.D: All of the above are true.

question: Which of the following is suitable for small meetings of an ordinary society?

options.B: Quasi committee of the whole
options.C: Informal consideration

question: Which statement is false regarding the informal consideration of a motion?

options.A: It is well suited for small meetings.
options.B: The regular presiding officer remains in the chair.
options.C: Members can only debate amendments one time.
options.D: The votes taken are recognized as decisions of the assembly.

question: During informal debate of a motion at a meeting, the "informal" aspect

options.A: limits the number of speeches allowed in debate.
options.B: removes the number of times members can debate.
options.C: allows debating without recognition from the chair.
options.D: allows members to ask several questions without recognition from the chair.

question: How would a member proceed to have the assembly go into a committee of the whole?

options.A: Ask the chairman to tell the assembly that they are now in a committee of the whole.
options.B: Propose a motion to go into a committee of the whole.
options.C: Obtain the floor and tell the assembly that they are now in a committee of the whole.
options.D: Request that the parliamentarian assume the chair for a committee of the whole.

question: Who is generally appointed by the presiding officer to assume the chair if a motion to refer to a committee of the whole is adopted?

options.B: Vice-president
options.C: Treasurer

question: The proceedings of a committee of the whole are

options.A: distributed to members for approval at the next regular meeting.
options.B: distributed to members.
options.C: not entered into the minutes of the assembly.
options.D: entered into the minutes of the assembly.

question: Which of the following should be included in the minutes of a regular meeting regarding a committee of the whole?

options.A: The actual motion of the referral to a committee of the whole
options.B: The report
options.C: The assembly's action on the report

question: A committee of the whole can

options.A: alter the text of any resolution referred to it.
options.B: adopt the same motions as if a regular assembly.
options.C: propose amendments and report them as recommendations to the assembly.
options.D: limit the number of times members may debate on a motion while it is considered by the committee.

question: Which of the following is false regarding the proceedings when the assembly is in a committee of the whole?

options.B: Motions to adjourn or to recess cannot be proposed.
options.C: A roll-call vote cannot be ordered.
options.D: A motion to close debate may be proposed anytime.

question: Unless prescribed in the bylaws, the quorum for a committee of the whole is

options.A: established by the committee as the first new business.
options.B: the same as that of the assembly.
options.C: always a majority of the committee members.
options.D: prescribed in the special bylaws drawn up by the committee.

question: If a committee of the whole lacks a quorum at any time, it must first

options.B: take measures to obtain a quorum.
options.C: rise and report the fact to the assembly.

question: What would you do as chairman if the motion below was proposed? MEMBER (After obtaining the floor):-"I move that the resolution be considered in quasi committee of the whole."

options.A: Ask for a second, ask for debate, and then take a vote on the motion.
options.B: Tell the member that the motion is not needed and that the pending motion will automatically go into a quasi committee of the whole if it is lost.
options.C: Ignore the motion.
options.D: Ask the vice-president to preside, and allow the assembly to go into a quasi committee of the whole.

question: In a quasi committee of the whole, each member is allowed to debate on motions

options.B: twice.
options.C: an unlimited number of times.

question: If an assembly considers a question informally, this means that

options.A: members can ask each other questions without going through the chairman.
options.B: debate is not allowed on all motions and their amendments.
options.C: there is no limit on the number of times members can speak in debate on main questions and their amendments.
options.D: members may debate longer than ten minutes each time they speak.

question: What should the assembly minutes show regarding the proceedings under informal consideration?

options.B: Include them in the minutes under "unfinished business."
options.C: Read, but do not include them in the minutes.

question: When a question is considered informally, as soon as it is disposed of

options.A: a motion must be proposed to stop the informal consideration.
options.B: the presiding officer turns the chair back to the president.
options.C: the informal consideration ceases automatically.

question: A mass meeting, as understood in parliamentary law, is a meeting of

options.A: an unorganized group called to take appropriate action on a specific problem.
options.B: all the clubs in an organization.
options.C: an organized society to draft its bylaws.
options.D: all the members of an organization to consider a specific problem.

question: Which one of the following types of meetings would not occur in an organized society?

options.B: Regular meeting
options.C: Annual meeting

question: One characteristic of a mass meeting is that they are

options.A: meetings of organized groups which must have bylaws.
options.B: called to only take action on a specific problem
options.C: only open to members over twenty-one years old.
options.D: bound by their bylaws to use Robert's Rules of Order.

question: One characteristic of a mass meeting is that the sponsors may

options.A: have the secretary read the minutes of the previous meeting immediately before unfinished business is taken up.
options.B: indicate the amount of dues after the meeting begins.
options.C: limit the right of attendance.
options.D: demand that they have a meeting at any time during the regular meeting of an organized society.

question: In a mass meeting, a standard parliamentary authority can be adopted by

options.A: the chairman before the meeting begins.
options.B: a majority vote on a motion from a member.
options.C: any group of three members before the meeting begins.
options.D: the officers during a recess of the meeting.

question: In a mass meeting, the officers that are generally elected are a chairman

options.B: and vice-president.
options.C: vice-president, and a secretary.

question: After the chairman is elected by a voice vote in a mass meeting, the next step for the chairman is to

options.A: state the reasons for the meeting.
options.B: read the names of the sponsors of the meeting.
options.C: conduct an election for a secretary.
options.D: divide the members into problem solving groups.

question: If you were the chairman of a mass meeting that was organized to oppose a new garbage dump in your neighborhood, and a member proposed a motion "to endorse the garbage dump location in the neighborhood," what would you do?

options.A: Ask for a second, ask for debate, and then vote on the motion.
options.B: Refer the motion to a special committee.
options.C: Call the motion out of order.
options.D: Ask the member to take the chair and explain the reasons for proposing the motion.

question: In a mass meeting, assembly members can generally speak

options.B: no longer than ten minutes at a time.
options.C: as long as desired.

question: It is advisable to have all committees at a mass meeting

options.A: selected by a voice vote of the members.
options.B: appointed by the chairman.
options.C: selected before the meeting opens.
options.D: assume their duties as prescribed in the bylaws of the mass meeting.

question: Unless a time has been set for another meeting at a mass meeting, a motion to adjourn is

options.B: permitted but must be adopted by a two-thirds vote of the assembly.
options.C: not in order while business is pending.

question: At a mass meeting, unless a time has been set for another meeting, the adoption of the motion to adjourn

options.A: allows members to go into their regular meeting.
options.B: dissolves the assembly.
options.C: temporarily postpones adjournment until members are notified by the secretary.

question: If the members at a mass meeting are trying to organize a permanent society and need to have more meetings, the presiding officer elected at the first meeting is designated as

options.B: "chairman."
options.C: "presiding officer."

question: The first business of a meeting to organize a permanent society is to

options.B: select a committee to choose the officers.
options.C: nominate a chairman pro tem and then a secretary.
options.D: adopt a resolution to form the society.

question: After a resolution to organize a society is adopted, the next step is usually the introduction and adoption of a motion

options.A: to fix the date of the next meeting.
options.B: that a committee be appointed by the chair to draft bylaws.
options.C: to authorize the secretary to duplicate copies of the minutes for approval at the next meeting.
options.D: to fix the hour and place of the next meeting.

question: The first draft of a newly organized society's bylaws are written by a

options.B: secretary pro tem.
options.C: committee.
options.D: chairman pro tem and secretary pro tem

question: The first item of business at the second organizational meeting in organizing a society is

options.A: consideration and adoption of the proposed bylaws.
options.B: the election of temporary officers.
options.C: selection of a permanent meeting site.
options.D: reading and approval of the minutes of the first meeting.

question: Members of a new society who sign a permanent record sheet that will be filed with the original papers of the organization are called

options.B: "Charter members."
options.C: "Permanent members."

question: When two existing societies wish to merge,

options.A: both continue to use their own bylaws.
options.B: one of the two continues, while the other ceases to exist.
options.C: both continue to use their own bylaws.
options.D: they must incorporate as a new society.

question: When two or more organizations merge or consolidate, the resulting organization

options.A: may be given a new name.
options.B: is required to have a new name.
options.C: must use parts of each group's name in the new name.
options.D: must use the word "incorporated" in the new name.

question: If an unincorporated society wishes to discontinue its existence, it should

options.B: adopt a resolution to rescind its bylaws.
options.C: adopt a motion to disband.
options.D: stop meeting, dispose of all records, and return its charter to the parent group.

category: How a Group Can Change Its Mind

question: The vote required to adopt a resolution to dissolve an unincorporated society is

options.A: a simple majority of the legal members present.
options.B: a unanimous vote by ballot.
options.C: the same vote required to adopt a secondary amendment.
options.D: the same as the vote and notice required to amend the bylaws.

question: A committee to draw up proposed bylaws should generally

options.B: include the president.
options.C: be large.
options.D: include the chairmen from all standing committees.

question: In writing bylaws, the committee should write each sentence

options.B: so it would be impossible to quote them out of context.
options.C: short and precise.
options.D: so that preceding or following sentences need to be used as a reference.

question: Bylaws of a new organization are adopted by a

options.B: majority vote.
options.C: unanimous consent.

question: The first article in an unincorporated society's bylaws lists the society's

options.B: name.
options.C: officers.

question: In forming a new, unincorporated society, Article II: Object of the bylaws should be

options.B: more than one sentence.
options.C: general.
options.D: should be written so that only the members can understand it.

question: Usually the article on members in the bylaws covers all of the following except

options.B: classes of members.
options.C: qualifications or eligibility of members.
options.D: the required fees and dues and the payable due dates.

question: All of the following should be included in Article IV: Officers of the bylaws except

options.A: the specific date new officers are to assume their duties.
options.B: how the officers will be elected.
options.C: the method of nominating officers.
options.D: the length of term of officers.

question: The bylaws should provide that the president should

options.A: not vote except to break a tie.
options.B: be listed first in the bylaw article listing the officers.
options.C: have his or her name listed in the bylaws.
options.D: stand while calling a meeting to order and while putting questions to a vote.

question: Under which bylaw article should provisions for methods of nominating officers be found?

options.B: Elections
options.C: Officers

question: How much of a term does an officer have to serve before it is considered a full term?

options.B: More than half
options.C: Three fourths

question: Which statement below is true regarding the contents of Article V: Meetings in the bylaws?

options.A: The annual meeting need not be specified.
options.B: Regular meeting days should be established.
options.C: The hour of the meetings should be fixed.
options.D: The quorum should not be established.

question: Article VI of the bylaws deals with the Executive Board (Board of Directors) and should include

options.A: details of the powers of the board.
options.B: the board's composition.
options.C: how often the board is to meet.

question: Article VII: Committees should provide all the following except

options.A: the names of the standing committees.
options.B: how standing committees are selected.
options.C: the composition and duties of standing committees.
options.D: the names of the special committees.

question: All of the following are typical examples of standing committees listed in bylaws except a

options.B: finance committee.
options.C: committee that was formed at a regular meeting to recommend a location for a picnic.

question: If Article VII provides that the president "shall be an ex-officio member of all committees except the Nominating Committee," this still means that the president

options.A: may not vote at committee meetings.
options.B: must attend committee meetings.
options.C: may debate at committee meetings.
options.D: cannot propose motions unless approved by the chairman at committee meetings.

question: If Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised is adopted as a society's parliamentary authority and another manual is in conflict with a specific point, which manual is binding?

options.A: The manual with the latest publication date.
options.B: They are both considered in committee, and a compromise decision is recommended and implemented.
options.C: Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised
options.D: The assembly votes on the manual to use for this specific controversy.

question: If the bylaws contain no provision for amending them, they can be amended by a

options.A: majority vote of the members present at any meeting.
options.B: special committee of the officers of the society.
options.C: two-thirds vote after notice at any business meeting.
options.D: two-thirds vote at any special meeting.

question: The articles of bylaws are divided into

options.B: sections.
options.C: segments.

question: If the meaning of a bylaw is not clear, it can be changed by

options.A: a unanimous vote of the members.
options.B: the chairman at a special meeting of the officers.
options.C: members through an amendment of the bylaws.

question: A motion to amend the bylaws should require at least a notice and a

options.B: two-thirds vote.
options.C: three-fourths vote.

question: A revision of bylaws can be perfected by

options.B: first and second degree amendments.
options.C: first, second, and third degree amendments.

question: When bylaw amendments conflict with one another, the vote

options.A: is first taken on the amendment which would be the most inclusive.
options.B: is first taken on the amendment which would be least inclusive.
options.C: order may be determined by the bylaws committee.
options.D: order is determined by the order in which the amendments were proposed.

question: If notice of a bylaw amendment is given at a meeting, it is usually under

options.B: unfinished business.
options.C: new business.

question: When notice has been given of a bylaw amendment, it becomes a general order

options.A: for the meeting at which it is to be considered.
options.B: and a special meeting must be called to consider it.
options.C: and is taken up under unfinished business at an executive meeting.
options.D: and is considered immediately after adjournment.

question: The time at which a bylaw amendment goes into effect is immediately upon

options.B: the conclusion of the report.
options.C: its adoption.
options.D: the signatures of all the officers.

question: While an amendment to a bylaw is pending, a motion can be made to amend it which requires a

options.B: two-thirds vote of members present and voting.
options.C: three-fourths vote of all members.
options.D: unanimous vote of the officers in executive session.

question: The adoption by a society of a proviso to a bylaw amendment requires

options.A: only a majority vote of the members present and voting.
options.B: a two-thirds vote of the members present and voting.
options.C: a three-fourths vote with previous notice.
options.D: no vote, since its adoption just requires unanimous agreement.

question: Corrections of bylaw articles or section numbers or cross references that cannot result in a change of meaning can be delegated to the

options.B: secretary or to a committee.
options.C: treasurer.

question: Delegates to a convention are usually chosen to represent their constituent units for one

options.B: session.
options.C: meeting.

question: Members of a society who are chosen especially for a convention as representatives within a larger group of people are called

options.B: representatives of a special committee.
options.C: delegates.

question: The term house of delegates or house of representatives applies to

options.A: delegates who are elected by a Corporation.
options.B: delegates attending a local convention.
options.C: delegates who are elected for a fixed term during which they hold sessions from time to time.
options.D: the voting members of a constituent club.

question: In an established state, regional, or national society composed of constituent parts, delegate qualifications should be prescribed

options.A: after the first meeting of the convention.
options.B: by the bylaws of the parent organization.
options.C: by individual units in their bylaws.

question: In an established state, regional, or national society, the bylaws of the parent body should

options.B: state the time and place for a periodic convention.
options.C: authorize a periodic convention.
options.D: fix the quorum for each unit.

question: What should the bylaws of the parent body of a convention prescribe for its delegates?

options.B: Qualifications
options.C: Method of electing

question: To avoid a change of officers during a convention, the bylaws should provide that newly elected officers should take up their duties

options.B: at the close of the convention.
options.C: at the beginning of the next convention.
options.D: after the beginning of the next calendar year.

question: In order for an alternate delegate to take the place of an elected delegate who has withdrawn, the alternate must register with the

options.B: parliamentarian.
options.C: credentials committee.

question: A delegate at a convention found out that she must miss the next business meeting. She asked her alternate to take her place. Is this proper?

options.A: Yes, but the alternate could not vote at the meeting.
options.B: No, unless the rules of the organization provide for it.
options.C: Only if the delegate agrees to attend and not speak on proposals.
options.D: Yes, the alternate delegate would have the same powers.

question: When a group of delegates meets during a convention to decide how they will act on certain matters that will come before the convention, it is called a (an)
